phenotype_specificity.statement: Elevated urinary GHB is stated for all patients (cohort-level); the patient's listed features are seizures, intellectual disability and motor delay. Exome sequencing was done, but the paper does not report results for other genes.

quotes.quote: As the gold-standard biomarker, elevated GHB was detected in all patients by urinary organic acids analysis.
Patients were diagnosed with SSADHD according to increased levels of GHB and the pathogenic variants in ALDH5A1, among whom patients 1 ~ 9 have been reported as clinical case series by us [13].
Whole exome sequencing was performed on DNA samples from the proband and/or parents.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Two-nucleotide deletion; the batch HGVS c.400_401del predicts p.(Asn134Ter), a premature stop at codon 134 in exon 2 (the paper places it in the NAD+ binding domain). The paper states a biallelic loss-of-function mechanism for this autosomal-recessive disorder.

quotes.quote: Autosomal-recessive disease follows a single mechanism: biallelic loss-of-function that leaves residual activity below the threshold required for normal physiology [29].

SSADHD—also known as 4-hydroxybutyric aciduria or γ-hydroxybutyric aciduria—is a rare autosomal-recessive disorder marked by markedly elevated levels of γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) and its metabolites [8].

concerns: Numbering: the paper writes c.398_399del (Supplementary Table 1: "c.398-399del"); the batch HGVS is NM_001080.3:c.400_401del. These may be the same deletion described at different positions in a repeat (3' shift), but the panel should confirm.
Protein differs (batch protein_check): the paper writes p.Q134*, while the protein predicted from the cDNA is p.(Asn134Ter). The paper's reference residue at 134 does not match the prediction.
Within-paper inconsistency on function: the text says the deletion "abolishes" protein and enzyme activity, while Table 1 lists an enzyme activity of 3.87 (%).
The paper counts "13 ALDH5A1 variants" in 12 probands in Results and "14 distinct variants" elsewhere (the 14 include two common SNPs and a variant from an extra, undiagnosed patient).
Methods state that patients 1 to 9 were reported earlier by the same group (ref. 13, a 2019 Chinese-language case series not in this batch); the same person may appear there.

Methods say both parents were Sanger sequenced to determine the variants' locations, but no per-parent genotype is reported for any patient; the compound-heterozygous label is therefore stated, not shown, in the text.
Supplementary Table 3 has a "Frequency" column (e.g. 1/26) whose denominator is not defined; it looks like a within-study count, not a population frequency, and should not be read as population data.
notes_for_panel: Transcript stated as NM_001080.3 in Methods. The other allele (c.638G>T, p.R213L) was also tested in the same assay (7.4% activity in Table 1).
